concepts.def: The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Coordination & Response — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Coordination & Response brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Coordination & Response.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a prokaryote?
options: Human skin cell
Yeast
Bacterium
Onion cell
protein synthesis
photosynthesis
aerobic respiration
cell division

mcqs.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right?
options: The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.
The left ventricle is thicker because it handles oxygenated blood, which is harder to pump.
It must pump blood at high pressure around the whole body; the right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs.
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?
options: Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells; meiosis produces four genetically different haploid cells (gametes).
Mitosis and meiosis both produce gametes; they are basically the same.
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.

mcqs.q: What does insulin do to blood glucose?
options: Insulin raises blood glucose to give the body energy.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
It lowers blood glucose by causing cells (especially liver and muscle) to take it up and store it as glycogen.

mcqs.q: A bacterium is 2 µm long. How many fit end-to-end across a 1 mm gap?
options: 500 bacteria
750 bacteria
250 bacteria
400 bacteria

mcqs.q: A bright light is shone into a person's eye and the pupil gets smaller without them thinking about it. This is best described as a:
options: Reflex action
Voluntary response
Hormonal response
Conscious decision

mcqs.q: A hormone is released into the blood but only the liver responds to it. Which best explains why?
options: Only liver cells have the specific receptor for that hormone.
The hormone is only carried to the liver by nerves.
The hormone is destroyed before reaching other organs.
All organs respond, but the liver responds first.

mcqs.q: Compared with a nervous response, a hormonal response is usually:
options: Slower to start but longer-lasting
Faster to start and shorter-lasting
Carried only along neurones
Always under conscious control

mcqs.q: In a reflex arc, what is the correct order the impulse travels?
options: Receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector
Effector → motor → relay → sensory → receptor
Receptor → motor → relay → sensory → effector
Sensory neurone → receptor → effector → motor neurone
